title: Rare-Event Tail Calibration and Distribution-Shift Stress Test
purpose: Evaluate fixed-threshold exceedance probability forecasts and conditional generalized-Pareto tail severity forecasts across in-distribution, temporal-shift, structural-dependency-shift and evidence-degradation regimes, with explicit importance-sampling weights and abstention accounting.
scope_limits: All cases, outcomes, probability forecasts, generalized Pareto parameters and sampling strata are fictional development data.
The fixture is intentionally stress-enriched. Unweighted event rates are not natural population prevalence estimates.

Importance weights are valid only for the declared routine/tail-enriched stratified sampling design; they do not correct model misspecification, within-stratum selection bias or unknown real-world prevalence.
The public cohort is a protocol/evaluator fixture, not an independently generated hidden test set.
A 128-case fixture cannot establish tail calibration, operational reliability, causal generalization or model superiority.
Tail calibration is distinct from overall calibration; a good overall proper score does not by itself establish reliable extreme-event forecasts.
The evaluator does not generate outages, make operational decisions, or infer causal mechanisms.

target.quantity: aggregate normalized service deficit-hours integrated over all declared critical services

regimes.qualification_note: time-ordered shifted regime; explicitly included and qualified for robustness testing
service dependency/common-cause structure shifted; explicitly included and qualified for robustness testing
evidence quality degraded; missing/conflicting inputs require abstention

sampling_design.design_note: 24 routine and 8 tail-enriched cases per regime; estimates target the declared 97%/3% stratum mixture only if cases are representative within their respective strata.

calibration_reference.description: Fictional historical training cohort used only to construct a fixed climatology comparison. It is not a real event base rate.

protocol.bin_convention: lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive; final bin includes 1.0
protocol.gpd_parameterization: conditional excess X=Y-u given Y>u; GPD CDF 1-(1+xi*x/sigma)^(-1/xi), exponential limit when xi=0
protocol.gpd_support: sigma>0; when xi<0, 0<=x< -sigma/xi; an observation outside forecast support is counted as zero-support/infinite conditional log loss
protocol.shift_comparison: report each regime separately and score deltas relative to in_distribution; do not aggregate away worst-slice failures
protocol.abstention_rule: qualification_state missing_critical_input, conflicting_sources or unsupported_distribution_shift requires action=abstain and null probability/GPD parameters
protocol.optional_abstention_rule: qualified cases may abstain only with reason=model_uncertainty; count against forecast coverage
protocol.risk_reporting: report raw case count, sum of importance weights, effective sample size and tail-event effective sample size for every regime

interpretation_guardrails: Candidate output is separate from evaluator-owned regime, qualification and observed severity.
Temporal and structural shifts are supported stress-test regimes and remain forecast-eligible unless an explicit unsupported state is supplied.
Missing, conflicting or unsupported evidence must never be converted into a zero event probability.
Report importance-weighted Brier/log-loss alongside unweighted case counts, forecast coverage, sum of weights and ESS.
Report tail occurrence calibration and conditional excess severity calibration separately.
A weighted tail-excess PIT distance is a diagnostic, not a p-value or proof of tail calibration.
A forecast that abstains on all cases is invalid; coverage must accompany selective scores.
No composite resilience, political, personal-suitability or leaderboard score is permitted.
